finding.claim: The /fetch2 endpoint fetches a user-supplied URL after only checking that the scheme is http or https. There is no host or IP filtering, and redirects are followed. An attacker can reach internal services, loopback and cloud metadata (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/), and can use an external redirect to the same targets.
finding.sink: requests.get(url, timeout=5) (views.py:22), which follows redirects by default

trace.note: url taken from the query string
requests.get(url) with redirects enabled, and the response body is returned to the caller

finding.guards_checked: is_http_url only validates the scheme. There is no hostname or IP allowlist or denylist, no private-range check, and no redirect restriction. Nothing else on the path blocks internal targets.

verdict.guard_found: none (is_http_url at validators.py:7 is scheme-only; the stronger is_safe_url is used only on /fetch, not /fetch2)
verdict.reason: views.py:19 takes the url from the query string, views.py:20 and validators.py:7 only check the scheme, and views.py:22 calls requests.get(url) with redirects on by default and returns the first 200 characters of the body, with no auth or middleware on the route.

finding.claim: The /fetch endpoint has a blocklist, but it is vulnerable to DNS rebinding (TOCTOU). is_safe_url resolves the hostname once to check it. requests.get then resolves it again, so an attacker-controlled DNS server can return a public IP for the check and an internal IP (127.0.0.1, 169.254.169.254) for the fetch. This is lower confidence than ssrf-1 because it needs an attacker-run DNS server with a short TTL.

trace.note: url taken from the query string
first DNS resolution via socket.getaddrinfo, and the resolved IPs are checked
private, loopback, link-local and reserved addresses are rejected
requests.get re-resolves the hostname independently, so the connected IP can differ from the validated one

finding.guards_checked: The scheme is restricted to http or https, and all resolved IPs are checked against private, loopback, link-local and reserved ranges. Redirects are disabled (allow_redirects=False), which blocks redirect-based bypass. The checked IP is not pinned to the connection, so the rebinding window remains.

verdict.guard_found: Scheme restriction (http/https) plus a resolved-IP blocklist (private/loopback/link-local/reserved) in validators.py:12-17, and allow_redirects=False at views.py:14. None of these pin the validated IP to the connection, and there is no host allowlist.
verdict.reason: views.py:12 validates via validators.py:14 getaddrinfo, then views.py:14 requests.get re-resolves the attacker-supplied host from views.py:11 with no IP pinning, so DNS rebinding (TOCTOU) bypasses the blocklist, which is not a closing guard.
